brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A green tea from the Shuangqiao area of Dawu county in Hubei.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was named a Chinese famous tea at a national assessment in 1989. Some accounts instead place a tea of this name in Hunan, and little more is documented about its past.
processing: Made in three stages: a first hot pan to kill the green, a second pan to soften and shape, then baking dry.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, downy strands of emerald green.
taste_profile: High, lasting aroma and a mellow, full taste with a lingering sweet return.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
